inputs.original_text: Angus Taylor has rejected Andrew Hastie’s call for the Liberals to be “open-minded” about raising taxes on gas companies and winding back property investor concessions, highlighting a clash between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. Taylor also stopped short of echoing Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump and would not say whether he supported the US and Israel’s war with Iran. The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership.
inputs.modified_text: Taylor is drawing a line against even discussing higher taxes on gas companies or reducing property investor concessions—exactly the sort of “open-minded” debate that might threaten powerful interests. His refusal to echo Hastie on Trump or say whether he supports the US and Israel’s war with Iran looks less like uncertainty than a careful effort to avoid upsetting people who matter. With MPs already talking about leadership, this is factional positioning dressed up as a policy clash: the party’s insiders are managing what can be questioned, and who gets to lead.
